Information since September points to continued labor-market tightening and solid real activity despite hurricane disruptions, while inflation remains below 2%. Read through the modern monetary-policy lens, this statement’s reliance on anchored expectations and a symmetric 2% objective is consistent with Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s New Keynesian framework in which rule-like behavior (e.g., Taylor-rule-consistent, gradual adjustments) stabilizes inflation and output. The Committee’s “gradual” path and interest-rate smoothing reinforce credibility, and the implementation details—maintaining IOER at 1.25% and operating ON RRP at 1.00%—fit Goodfriend’s (2002) advocacy for interest-on-reserves/corridor-style control of the policy rate. With real-side momentum and accommodative financial conditions supporting business investment (in line with the Bernanke–Gertler credit channel), but market-based inflation compensation still low, the overall tone is cautiously positive rather than exuberant.
